**What changed:** `NgTemplateOutlet` (selector `[ngTemplateOutlet]`, `@angular/common`) gained a new `@Input() ngTemplateOutletInjector: Injector | 'outlet' | null | undefined`. Previously the input only accepted an `Injector` instance (or null/undefined, in which case no injector was passed to `ViewContainerRef.createEmbeddedView`). Now the literal string `'outlet'` may be bound, and the directive resolves it to its own injected `Injector` (`protected injector = inject(Injector)`), so the embedded view inherits the injector of the outlet's location in the instantiated DOM rather than an explicitly supplied one or the declaration-site default. Changing `ngTemplateOutletInjector` (including switching to/from `'outlet'`) causes the embedded view to be destroyed and re-created (`_shouldRecreateView` checks `ngTemplateOutlet` and `ngTemplateOutletInjector`) (https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/18003a33bb0d6bb09def8a0e5939fa24069696eb, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/angular/angular/18003a33bb0d6bb09def8a0e5939fa24069696eb/packages/common/src/directives/ng_template_outlet.ts).

**Affects:** Only additive — applications using `*ngTemplateOutlet` / `[ngTemplateOutletInjector]` are unaffected unless they opt in. Note the pre-existing behavior that any change to `ngTemplateOutletInjector` re-creates the view.

**Action:** none (opt-in feature: bind `ngTemplateOutletInjector="outlet"` where the embedded view should resolve dependencies from the outlet's DOM position.)

**Before/after:**
```html
<!-- old: an explicit Injector object only -->
<ng-container
  *ngTemplateOutlet="template; context: ctx; injector: injector"></ng-container>

<!-- new (21.2): inherit the injector from the outlet's location in the DOM -->
<ng-container
  *ngTemplateOutlet="template; context: ctx; injector: 'outlet'"></ng-container>
```

**What changed:** Angular's template expression parser gained the JavaScript `instanceof` binary operator, which previously was listed among *unsupported* operators and produced a template parse error. Commit `72534e2a34` ("feat(compiler): Add support for the `instanceof` binary operator", fixes #59975) added `instanceof` to the `KEYWORDS` array and a new `Token.isKeywordInstanceOf()` method in `packages/compiler/src/expression_parser/lexer.ts`, added `'instanceof'` to the `BinaryOperation` union in `ast.ts`, handled it in `parseRelational()` in `parser.ts` (same precedence tier as `<`, `>`, `<=`, `>=`, `in`), and added `BinaryOperator.InstanceOf` to `packages/compiler/src/output/output_ast.ts`, wired through `abstract_emitter.ts` and the template pipeline's `BINARY_OPERATORS` map in `packages/compiler/src/template/pipeline/src/conversion.ts` ((https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/72534e2a3458df4e1bb097973872f00bbb92be42)). On the `compiler-cli` side, `instanceof` was added to the `BinaryOperator` string union in `ngtsc/translator/src/api/ast_factory.ts` (mapped to `ts.SyntaxKind.InstanceOfKeyword` in `typescript_ast_factory.ts`) and to the operator map in `ngtsc/typecheck/src/expression.ts`, so it participates in template type checking (invalid uses produce diagnostics such as `The left-hand side of an 'instanceof' expression must be of type 'any', an object type or a type parameter.`). The docs table in `adev/src/content/guide/templates/expression-syntax.md` moved `instanceof` (`car instanceof Automobile`) from "Unsupported operators" to "Supported operators" (also visible at https://raw.githubusercontent.com/angular/angular/main/adev/src/content/guide/templates/expression-syntax.md). It works in any template expression — interpolation, bindings, event statements and built-in control flow blocks such as `@if(myObject instanceof SomeClass)` (https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/59975). Note: in the emitted code the right-hand side is resolved as a *member of the component/directive context* (`$ctx$.Bar instanceof $ctx$.Bar`), so the constructor/class must be exposed as a property, as in the compliance test `Bar = Bar;`.

**Affects:** Nothing for existing apps — purely additive; only templates that previously failed to parse because they used `instanceof` (or that worked around it with precomputed booleans, custom pipes, or structural directives) are affected. Requires Angular 21.2 to compile templates that use it.

**Action:** none. Optionally, replace workarounds (component-computed booleans like `isSomeClass = myObject instanceof SomeClass`, or custom pipes) with direct `instanceof` expressions in templates.

**Before/after:**
```html
<!-- Before (21.1): parse error - instanceof unsupported -->
@if (myObject instanceof SomeClass) { Content for SomeClass instance. }

<!-- After (21.2): supported in expressions -->
{{ bar instanceof Bar }}
<button (click)="number += 1"></button>
```
(templates from the commit: `packages/compiler-cli/test/compliance/test_cases/r3_view_compiler/operators.ts` and issue #59975)

**What changed:** Angular 21.2 extends the existing extended diagnostic `uninvoked_function_in_event_binding` (in `packages/compiler-cli/src/ngtsc/typecheck/extended/checks/uninvoked_function_in_event_binding/index.ts`) so that an event listener whose bound expression is an `ArrowFunction` (AST node from `@angular/compiler`) is now flagged as a no-op, since arrow functions became legal in Angular expressions (21.2 feature, PR #66294) but writing `(click)="() => expr"` never invokes the function. The build now emits a `ts.DiagnosticCategory.Warning` with code `ngErrorCode(ErrorCode.UNINVOKED_FUNCTION_IN_EVENT_BINDING)` and message "Arrow function will not be invoked in this event listener. Did you intend to call a method?" (https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/2ea6dfc6c9ca11e96a2654510c980419899f8d04)

**Affects:** Applications with templates that bind an arrow function directly in an event listener (e.g. `(click)="() => 123"`); the check runs under template type-checking extended diagnostics in `compiler-cli`. New warnings only — no runtime or compilation behavior changes otherwise.

**Action:** required: re-verify builds after upgrade for new `UNINVOKED_FUNCTION_IN_EVENT_BINDING` warnings, and fix any flagged listeners by invoking a real method or expression (e.g. `(click)="expr"`) instead of a no-op arrow function.

**Before/after:**
```html
<!-- Warns in 21.2: arrow function is never invoked -->
<button (click)="() => 123"></button>

<!-- Intent was likely: -->
<button (click)="123"></button>
```

**What changed:** Angular 21.2.0 adds `ChangeDetectionStrategy.Eager = 1` to the `ChangeDetectionStrategy` enum in `@angular/core` (`packages/core/src/change_detection/constants.ts`), as an explicit alias for `ChangeDetectionStrategy.Default = 1`, which is now marked `@deprecated Use Eager instead.` (`Eager`: "the component is checked eagerly when the change detection traversal reaches it, rather than only checking under certain circumstances (e.g. `markForCheck`, a signal in the template changed, etc)") (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/angular/angular/8d5210c9fedd8abdd810d7a89ec7ee9a1234f5c1/packages/core/src/change_detection/constants.ts, https://angular.dev/api/core/ChangeDetectionStrategy). The two members share enum value `1` (a duplicate enum value, suppressed with `// tslint:disable-next-line:no-duplicate-enum-values`), so behaviour is identical: the compiler resolves the member by value in `resolveEnumValue` (`packages/compiler-cli/src/ngtsc/annotations/common/src/evaluation.ts`), and at runtime `defineComponent` (`packages/core/src/render3/definition.ts`) only special-cases `changeDetection === ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush` (0), so `1` yields eager checking (`onPush: false`) (https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/8d5210c9fedd8abdd810d7a89ec7ee9a1234f5c1).

**Affects:** Components setting `changeDetection: ChangeDetectionStrategy.Default` (may now see deprecation warnings) or wanting the explicit `Eager` spelling. No behavioural change; existing `Default` usages keep working.

**Action:** none (optional: switch `changeDetection: ChangeDetectionStrategy.Default` to `ChangeDetectionStrategy.Eager` to avoid the deprecation). Note that because both members have value `1`, code that reads the enum value or reverse-maps `1` may now see either name.

**Before/after:**
```typescript
export enum ChangeDetectionStrategy {
  OnPush = 0,

  /**
   * @deprecated Use `Eager` instead.
   */
  Default = 1,

  // tslint:disable-next-line:no-duplicate-enum-values
  Eager = 1,
}
```

**What changed:** Angular 21.2.0 adds support for arrow functions inside Angular template expressions (interpolations, bindings, event handlers, host bindings/listeners, `@let`, and pipes). Arrow functions behave like JS arrow functions with the same access as other Angular expressions, subject to two limitations: only implicit-return forms are allowed (`(a) => a + 1` is valid, `(a) => { return a + 1 }` is not), and pipes cannot be used inside an arrow function body, though an arrow function itself can be passed through a pipe (commit d9923b72a2). To avoid recreating functions each change detection, the compiler extracts parameter-only arrow functions into a top-level constant, and stores context-capturing arrow functions on the current view (https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/d9923b72a20972ba6bf728d78f1afac6936ade18, .diff). Supported forms shown in the compiler test cases include signal updates like `sigA.update(value => value + 1)`, IIFEs like `{{((a, b) => a + this.a + b + this.b)(1, 3)}}`, `@let fn = (a, b) => componentValue + a + b;`, host bindings such as `'[attr.with-context]': '((a, b) => a / b + componentProp)(6, 12)'`, and currying like `(a => b => c => d => a + b + c + d)(1)(2)(3)(4)` (https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/d9923b72a20972ba6bf728d78f1afac6936ade18.diff). Motivating use case from issue #14129: inline predicate functions for `@angular/forms` `compareWith` (https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/14129).

**Affects:** All applications — this is additive syntax support; previously arrow function syntax in templates was a compile error, and no existing valid expression changes meaning.

**Action:** none (optionally: newly possible to replace component-declared predicate/lambdas with inline arrow functions in templates).

**Before/after:**
```html
<!-- Before: predicate must be declared on the component -->
<select [compareWith]="equals" [(ngModel)]="selectedCountries">

<!-- After (Angular 21.2): inline arrow function in the expression -->
<select [compareWith]="(a, b) => a.id == b.id" [(ngModel)]="selectedCountries">
```
(from https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/14129)

**What changed:** The AI-development-context best-practices documentation bundled with `@angular/core` no longer tells models to avoid arrow functions in templates. The line `- Do not write arrow functions in templates (they are not supported).` was deleted from `packages/core/resources/best-practices.md` and from `adev/src/context/guidelines.md`, because arrow functions are now supported in templates (commit `ed78fa05c7`, "fix(core): Remove note to skip arrow functions in best practices", by Andrew Scott) (https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/ed78fa05c710ebafb355ae00a85b190a118b6cc4.patch). No runtime/API code was modified; the diff is 2 deletions in two Markdown files only.

**Affects:** Applications that feed these bundled best-practice prompts (e.g. the `best-practices.md` context file shipped in `packages/core/resources`) to AI coding assistants or code generators; no application code or build behavior changes.

**Action:** none — no application code, configuration, or dependency change is required. Optionally re-verify that AI-generated templates produced with the updated context (which may now contain arrow functions in templates) compile correctly.

**Before/after:**
```markdown
- Use built in pipes and import pipes when being used in a template, ...
- Do not assume globals like (`new Date()`) are available.
-- Do not write arrow functions in templates (they are not supported).   # removed
```

**What changed:** The `feat(forms)` capability allows defining default submit options at the form level via `FormOptions`. This updates the API to accept a submission configuration object when creating the form (via `ngFormOptions` in Template-driven forms or `AbstractControlOptions` in Reactive forms), which serves as defaults for properties like `action` and validation behavior during `submit()`. This behavior can be overridden at the call site if specific options are provided to the `submit` method (https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/95ecce8334299defe55fb2b74264e5258ffd137c).
**Affects:** Applications using Angular Forms that require customized form submission behavior (e.g., custom HTTP methods or actions) or applications utilizing form-level options.
**Action:** none (optional: update form configuration to use new `FormOptions` or `AbstractControlOptions` to centralize submission settings).
**Before/after:**
```html
<!-- Template-driven: form-level options in ngFormOptions -->
<form [ngFormOptions]="{updateOn: 'blur'}">
  <input name="one" ngModel>
</form>
```

**What changed:** Signal-forms native number inputs (`<input type=number>` bound with a `signalModel`/model) now support `null` as a model value (21.2.0, PR #66917). Binding `null` clears the input; binding `NaN` also clears it. When the user clears the input, the model is set to `null` (previously the value surfaced as `NaN`). The model is _never_ set to `NaN` from user interaction: an un-parsable entry such as `"42e"` leaves the model unchanged and reports the failure through the new `parseErrors` API integrated into native inputs. A companion fix in the same PR changed `parsedErrors` to a `linkedSignal` derived from the model value, so parse errors are reset when the model is updated from outside the control (https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/30f09147545b67185f93efb9796e37c1db76733a, https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/22afbb2f36be89c2ae575df343571a918dec5985, https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/27397b3f4f3182ce00d6e2f8690285c316e2a274, https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/66917).

**Affects:** Applications using signal-forms native inputs bound to a number-typed model, especially code that previously read `NaN` for a cleared number input or that set `NaN` deliberately to clear the field.

**Action:** required: re-verify number-input handling — replace any `NaN` comparisons / `NaN` assignments on number models with `null` (a cleared input now yields `null`), and handle invalid user input by reading the control's parse errors instead of expecting the model to change. Also re-verify that parse errors disappear when the model is set programmatically.

**Before/after:**
No code snippet is shown on the fetched commit/PR pages; the behaviour is described only in prose: "Binding in `null` clears the input … When the user clears the input, the model is set to `null` … The model is _never_ set to `NaN` based on user interaction. It is either set to `null` if the user cleared the input, or is unchanged and a parse error added if the user entered an invalid number like \"42e\"" (https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/30f09147545b67185f93efb9796e37c1db76733a).

**What changed:** In signal-forms native `<input type=number>` handling, the internal `parsedErrors` state was changed to a `linkedSignal` derived from the model value, so parse errors are automatically reset when the model changes from outside the control (e.g. code setting `ctrl.set(...)`), rather than persisting until the next user interaction (https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/27397b3f4f3182ce00d6e2f8690285c316e2a274). This is part of the parse-errors work in PR #66917, where native inputs report `parseErrors` when the user types an un-parsable value like "42e": the model then retains its previous value and a parse error is added for the control; binding `null` or `NaN` clears a number input, clearing the input sets the model to `null`, and the model is never set to `NaN` by user interaction (https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/66917, https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/22afbb2f36be89c2ae575df343571a918dec5985, https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/30f09147545b67185f93efb9796e37c1db76733a).

**Affects:** Applications using signal forms with native number inputs that display or rely on parse errors while also updating the control's model programmatically.

**Action:** none — no code changes required; re-verify that UIs showing parse errors clear correctly when the model is updated programmatically, and that number inputs do not linger on stale parse errors.

**What changed:** In signal forms (`@angular/forms/signals`), the `FormField` directive (selector `[formField]`) now adds a dev-mode `effect` that checks `this.state()` as a `FieldNode` and, when `fieldNode.hidden()` is true, calls `console.warn` with a new runtime error code `RENDERED_HIDDEN_FIELD = 1916` (added in `packages/forms/signals/src/errors.ts`) and the message: `Field '<path>' is hidden but is being rendered. Hidden fields should be removed from the DOM using @if.` (path comes from `fieldNode.structure.pathKeys().join('.')`, falling back to `'<root>'`) (https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/d75046bc091699bbadcb5f2032be627e983ee6fa). The user is still responsible for guarding hidden fields in the template; no behaviour change other than the warning. The same commit also hardened two existing `RuntimeError` messages (`BINDING_ALREADY_REGISTERED = 1913`, `INVALID_FIELD_DIRECTIVE_HOST = 1914`) to guard `ngDevMode` with `typeof ngDevMode !== 'undefined'`.

**Affects:** Applications using signal forms with a `hidden(...)` logic rule on a field whose `[formField]` host element is not wrapped in a conditional template block, running in dev mode. No production behaviour change; warning only.

**Action:** none — required only if the new dev-mode warning appears: wrap the hidden field's host element in `@if (!f().hidden()) { ... }` so it is removed from the DOM when hidden.

**Before/after:**
```html
<!-- before: warns in dev when hidden(p, ...) is true -->
<input [formField]="f" />

<!-- after: no warning, guarded in template -->
@if (!f().hidden()) {
  <input [formField]="f" />
}
```

**What changed:** The Angular language server (shipped with the VS Code extension) now implements the LSP `onDidChangeWatchedFiles` notification, letting the client tell the server about file changes instead of the server creating its own system file/directory watchers (`watchFile`/`watchDirectory` are stubbed via a new `ServerHost` implementation) (https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/6fb39d9b62cbb634e95ec00fe5ef85d84da3bdbd). The behaviour is opt-in via the new VS Code setting `angular.server.useClientSideFileWatcher`; when enabled, the extension registers a `FileSystemWatcher` for `.ts`, `.html`, and `package.json` files and forwards events to the server. Benefits stated in the commit: no duplicated watchers, no OS watcher-handle limits (`ENOSPC`), use of VS Code's optimized native watcher (Parcel Watcher), client-side debouncing of event floods (e.g. during `git checkout`), and roughly 10-50x faster initialization observed in a very large internal project. This addressed issue #66543, where the extension appeared stuck initializing.

**Affects:** Developers using the Angular Language Service VS Code extension (editor tooling only); no application build, runtime, or Angular template/API code is affected.

**Action:** none — this is an opt-in editor performance improvement. Optionally set `angular.server.useClientSideFileWatcher` in VS Code settings to enable client-side watching; re-verify that the Angular language service initializes and reports diagnostics correctly with it enabled.

Before/after: no code or configuration snippet is shown in the fetched page.

**What changed:** `RouterLinkActive.routerLinkActiveOptions`, `Router.isActive`, and the standalone `isActive` function now accept `Partial<IsActiveMatchOptions>` instead of a full `IsActiveMatchOptions`. Missing properties fall back to `subsetMatchOptions` defaults: `paths: 'subset'`, `queryParams: 'subset'`, `matrixParams: 'ignored'`, `fragment: 'ignored'` (implementation merges `{...subsetMatchOptions, ...matchOptions}`) (https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/907a94dcec2926a5c7d0c4d36249bd62e31a2ae3.patch). Updated public signatures: `export function isActive(url: string | UrlTree, router: Router, matchOptions?: Partial<IsActiveMatchOptions>): Signal<boolean>;`, `isActive(url: string | UrlTree, matchOptions: Partial<IsActiveMatchOptions>): boolean;` (deprecated since 21.1 in favor of the `isActive` function), and `@Input() routerLinkActiveOptions: {exact: boolean} | Partial<IsActiveMatchOptions> = {exact: false};`. The internal `isActiveMatchOptions` type guard now checks any of `paths || matrixParams || queryParams || fragment` instead of only `paths` (same patch). Fixes #53326 (https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/53326).

**Affects:** Applications that pass `routerLinkActiveOptions`, `Router.isActive`, or `isActive` match options; purely additive — previously required full option objects still compile and behave identically.

**Action:** none — existing code keeps working; optionally simplify option objects to only the properties you need. Note one behavioral edge case: an options object containing none of `paths`, `matrixParams`, `queryParams`, `fragment` (e.g. `{}`) is now treated like the `{exact: ...}` form rather than as match options.

**Before/after:**
```html
<!-- Before: all options required -->
<a routerLinkActive="active"
   [routerLinkActiveOptions]="{queryParams: 'ignored', matrixParams: 'exact', paths: 'exact', fragment: 'ignored'}">

<!-- After: only what you need; others default to subset/ignored -->
<a routerLinkActive="active" [routerLinkActiveOptions]="{paths: 'exact'}">
```
